title: Removal of Corrosion from Metallic Airframe Structure and Restoration of the Protective Treatment
abstract: General procedure for classifying and removing corrosion from metallic airframe structure, with the mechanical and chemical methods permitted for each severity level and the chromated treatment that restores the protection.

sections.purpose: This task gives the general method for classifying corrosion on metallic airframe structure, removing it inside the allowable limits, and restoring the protective treatment so that the structure returns to a serviceable condition.
sections.job_setup_note: Classify the corrosion before you choose a removal method: light surface corrosion may be removed with abrasive nylon, moderate corrosion needs mechanical removal with a rotary tool, and severe or intergranular corrosion is always outside this task. Establish the nominal thickness and the allowable removal depth for the item from the structural repair data before you touch it. Never use a steel wire brush on aluminium.
sections.procedure: 1. Clean the area and remove the paint scheme to expose the full extent of the corrosion. 2. Classify the corrosion as light, moderate or severe using the criteria in the referenced data. 3. Where the corrosion is severe or intergranular, stop and raise a repair request. 4. Measure and record the thickness of the item at five points around the damage. WARNING: SOME STRUCTURE IN THIS ZONE IS THIN AND CARRIES PRIMARY LOAD. DO NOT START REMOVAL BEFORE YOU HAVE THE ALLOWABLE DEPTH IN WRITING. 5. For light corrosion, remove the product with an abrasive nylon pad and an approved cleaner. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH ON ALUMINIUM. EMBEDDED STEEL PARTICLES WILL START GALVANIC CORROSION. 6. For moderate corrosion, remove the material with a rotary tool and fair the edges at a ratio of 20 to 1. 7. Measure the remaining thickness and compare it with the allowable. 8. Polish the removal area and do a dye penetrant inspection where the item is fatigue critical. 9. Apply the chromated conversion coating and the chromated primer to all bare metal and let them cure. 10. Where the splice plate D5120121576256 or the shear tie D5120122733685 is affected, apply the extended protection scheme given for the joint area. 11. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound and restore the paint scheme.
sections.close_out: Record the classification, the removal depth and the remaining thickness on the aircraft corrosion record with a sketch of the affected area. Remove the tools and the waste from the area. Where the item is on a repeat corrosion inspection, confirm that the next due date has been recalculated from this removal.

safety_precautions: Wear eye protection and a dust mask during mechanical removal.
Do not use a steel wire brush on aluminium.
Use penetrant and developer only in a ventilated area.
Do not start removal without the written allowable depth.

tooling.description: Rotary tool set with aluminium burrs
Ultrasonic thickness gauge with 5 MHz probe

title: Removal of Corrosion from Metallic Airframe Structure and Restoration of the Protective Treatment

issue.reason: The restoration step names the replacement protection process and its cure condition in place of the withdrawn chromated treatment.

abstract: General procedure for classifying and removing corrosion from metallic airframe structure, with the methods permitted for each severity level and the chromate-free process that now restores the protection.

sections.purpose: This task gives the general method for classifying corrosion on metallic airframe structure, removing it inside the allowable limits, and restoring the protective treatment so that the structure returns to a serviceable condition.
sections.job_setup_note: Classify the corrosion before you choose a removal method: light surface corrosion may be removed with abrasive nylon, moderate corrosion needs mechanical removal with a rotary tool, and severe or intergranular corrosion is always outside this task. Establish the nominal thickness and the allowable removal depth for the item from the structural repair data before you touch it. Never use a steel wire brush on aluminium. The chromated treatment named in earlier issues of this task is withdrawn and is no longer obtainable; the restoration step now calls up the chromate-free process, and a station that cannot run that process must not start the removal, because the structure would be left as bare prepared metal with no compliant way of protecting it. Check the aircraft against the aft cabin work package before you plan the visit: the enlarged potable water tank cradle of MOD-153504 covers structure that this task inspects and restores and is not removable once installed, so where both fall in the same window this task is completed and signed off before the tank is fitted.
sections.procedure: 1. Clean the area and remove the paint scheme to expose the full extent of the corrosion. 2. Classify the corrosion as light, moderate or severe using the criteria in the referenced data. 3. Where the corrosion is severe or intergranular, stop and raise a repair request. 4. Measure and record the thickness of the item at five points around the damage. WARNING: SOME STRUCTURE IN THIS ZONE IS THIN AND CARRIES PRIMARY LOAD. DO NOT START REMOVAL BEFORE YOU HAVE THE ALLOWABLE DEPTH IN WRITING. 5. For light corrosion, remove the product with an abrasive nylon pad and an approved cleaner. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH ON ALUMINIUM. EMBEDDED STEEL PARTICLES WILL START GALVANIC CORROSION. 6. For moderate corrosion, remove the material with a rotary tool and fair the edges at a ratio of 20 to 1. 7. Measure the remaining thickness and compare it with the allowable. 8. Polish the removal area and do a dye penetrant inspection where the item is fatigue critical. 9. Restore the protection with the chromate-free system: apply the trivalent chromium conversion coating and then the chromate-free epoxy primer to all bare metal, following task AMM-Z-51-20-11-100-005-A, and cure the primer for the full period at the temperature given there. Do not substitute a chromated product. 10. Where the splice plate D5120121576256 or the shear tie D5120122733685 is affected, apply the extended protection scheme given for the joint area. 11. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound and restore the paint scheme.
sections.close_out: Record the classification, the removal depth, the remaining thickness and the protection process used on the aircraft corrosion record with a sketch of the affected area. Remove the tools and the waste from the area. Where the item is on a repeat corrosion inspection, confirm that the next due date has been recalculated from this removal. Where the structure has since been covered by a tank cradle, record that fact against the item so that the next due date is raised as a planning conflict rather than as a routine task.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; the restoration step uses the chromate-free process only

Do not use a steel wire brush on aluminium.
